work_orders.objective:
Assumptions
- Runs as a lightweight background daemon with Unix domain socket / named pipe IPC on macOS, Linux, and Windows (WSL).
- Target user is an engineer or power user interacting via standard terminal emulators, multiplexers (tmux, zellij), or native CLI commands.
- Model integration supports standard provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, local LLMs) with Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool discovery and execution.
Core Capabilities
- Cross-Session Agent Bus
  - Lightweight background daemon managing agent runtimes and shared state
  - Inter-process message broker allowing CLI/TUI sessions to broadcast and receive agent events
  - Context synchronization across active terminal panes, shells, and background tasks
- Model & Tool Layer
  - Model-agnostic engine supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
  - Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) client support for plug-and-play tool integration
  - Configurable system prompts, streaming responses, and token budget management
- TUI & CLI Interfaces
  - Headless daemon mode with lightweight CLI client for inline shell commands
  - Optional interactive TUI panel for monitoring active agents, chat streams, and session logs
  - Multiplexer integration hooks (tmux / zellij status bars and pane spawners)
Data
- Session history, agent states, and conversation logs stored locally in SQLite or structured JSON/JSONL.
- Configuration (endpoints, MCP servers, key bindings, defaults) stored in standard user config paths (~/.config/tui-agent-workspace/config.toml).
- Sensitive credentials loaded via environment variables or native system keyrings.
Deliverables
- Core daemon engine with socket IPC and message bus.
- CLI command suite (query, listen, send, status, stop).
- Interactive TUI client for live agent monitoring and chat.
- MCP client runtime and LLM provider adapter suite.
- Comprehensive configuration template and shell integration scripts.
Future Expansion
- Remote multi-node agent mesh for cross-machine orchestration.
- Custom plugin ecosystem for IDE integration (Neovim / VS Code extensions).
- Fine-grained permission profiles per agent role.
Integrations
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers for file inspection, shell execution, git, and custom extensions.
- Local and cloud LLM providers (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Ollama local models).
- Terminal multiplexer hooks and shell integrations (bash, zsh, fish).
Objective
- Build an extensible terminal-native agent workspace that allows multiple independent terminal sessions and TUI tools to share context, coordinate agent actions, and communicate seamlessly via a unified IPC daemon.
Project
- OS/TUI/model agnostic workspace enabling native TUI workflows and cross-session agent communication.
Safety & Constraints
- Tool execution approval gates: interactive confirmation prompts for destructive shell or filesystem actions.
- Local-first data privacy: conversation context and session logs never leave the local machine except when calling configured LLM APIs.
- Graceful socket cleanup and lock handling to prevent stale daemon instances.
User Experience
- Users launch the daemon or let it auto-spawn on first CLI/TUI invocation.
- Any terminal window can send prompts, pipe command output, or listen to agent events via simple CLI commands or dedicated TUI views.
- Agents can notify other sessions when background tasks complete or request user confirmation before tool execution.
